end.summary:
Ishita practised drawing dot pictures for square and triangular numbers; easy questions were right, with a why or new-situation question still to check.
Ishita practised showing sequence growth by adding a new row or column; easy questions were right, with a why or new-situation question still to check.
They practised counting the shared corner once when combining a row and column.
A total was first stated as 27, then corrected later to 28; the 20/19 count was also corrected to 19.
end.parentNote: Asha practised square and triangular dot pictures with Ishita, including how a sequence grows by adding a row or column. Ishita used the shared-corner method to avoid counting one dot twice; the 27 total was corrected to 28 later in the lesson, and the 20 total was corrected to 19. At home, draw a few growing dot pictures and ask Ishita to explain why the shared corner is counted once; a new example can be checked next time.
